title: Shoulder reduction under procedural sedation
stem: Resus 4. Mr Lui, 17, dislocated his left shoulder falling while skateboarding. The X-ray confirms an anterior dislocation without fracture. Consent has been obtained. Demonstrate how you would reduce it under procedural sedation.

phases.title: Set up
phases.goal: Monitoring, airway kit, access, two clinicians, and reversal drugs ready.

phases.title: Neurovascular check
phases.goal: Before you touch it: the axillary nerve and the hand.

phases.title: Sedate
phases.goal: From the cart: analgesia, then a titrated sedative.

phases.title: Reduce
phases.goal: A gentle technique, then re-check and recover.

notes:
Checked against RCEM/RCoA 'Safe sedation of adults in the ED' (2012, RCEM 2019 update), and evidence on reduction techniques (Cunningham, external rotation, FARES, Spaso, Milch, Kocher).

Safety: resus bay, two clinicians (a sedationist separate from the person reducing), monitoring (SpO2, ECG, NIBP, capnography), oxygen, suction, airway kit, reversal agents. Neurovascular check before (axillary nerve badge sensation and deltoid; radial, median, ulnar motor; radial pulse) and after. Sedation: titrate, e.g. midazolam 0.02–0.1 mg/kg with fentanyl 0.5–1 microgram/kg, or propofol, or ketamine 1–2 mg/kg; aim for deep enough relaxation (your notes use the modified Ramsay score 4–5). Many dislocations reduce without sedation (Cunningham, external rotation), which avoids sedation risk.

Kocher's method carries a higher risk of fracture and nerve injury (your notes say so). After reduction: X-ray, sling, recovery observation until the discharge criteria are met, written advice. Your notes on doses, techniques and signs of reduction match this.

Perfect script checked against the RCEM/ICM procedural sedation guidance, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the tenfold doses; the benches narrated.

cards.q: After reduction, the X-ray looks for…
options: Congruent joint and fractures (Hill-Sachs, Bankart, greater tuberosity)
Lung pathology such as a pneumothorax
Asleep, rouses to a loud voice or tap
Unresponsive, even to a firm trapezius squeeze
cards.why: Target for reduction per your notes.

script.say: SpO2, ECG, NIBP and capnography on. Oxygen, suction, bag-valve-mask and airway adjuncts at the bedside. IV cannula in the other arm.
Dr Kwan runs the sedation; I do the reduction.
Naloxone and flumazenil naloxone 400 microgram and flumazenil 200 microgram, drawn up and labelled.
Before anyone touches the shoulder: sensation over the badge area for the axillary nerve; wrist and finger extension, thumb opposition, finger spread; the radial pulse.
Fentanyl 1 microgram/kg (70 microgram) IV. Midazolam 1–2 mg IV, titrated in small doses.

Is he sedated enough? Dr Kwan on the airway. Slow external rotation with the elbow at his side, holding the rotation, then gentle abduction: a clunk, and the shoulder contour returns. Then the nerves again, a sling, a check X-ray, and recovery observation.
